assumptions: Annealing follows pydna's rule; dimer free energies are primer3 thal's at the stated conditions.
limits: Predicts products and interactions, not the yields that decide a multiplex on the bench.
Products are those the templates given can make; a genome may hold others.
bio.jane/contract.question: What does a primer pool do on these templates: products, off-target binding, template-distinguishing pairs, and the dimer matrix?

description: Screen a primer POOL against one or more templates: every predicted product, per-primer off-target binding, the pairs that tell templates apart on a gel, and the all-against-all primer-dimer matrix a pool actually lives or dies by (pydna primer_screen + primer3 thal).

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

conditions.description: the reaction buffer every temperature here is computed in - Na+/K+/Tris/Mg2+/dNTPs, the primer concentration, the salt-correction method and the melting model. Left unset it is filled from your reaction-conditions settings, so this node and the PCR panel describe ONE tube; with neither it falls back to pydna's Taq defaults, which is what every golden was captured under. Advanced.

cutoff_max_prim_prim_any_tm.description: Cross-dimer Tm, anywhere [°C]: primer3's own limit, on the scale our ΔG engine is calibrated for. A dimer melting above this competes with template annealing. Unset keeps the preset's value. In °C. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_max_prim_prim_end_tm.description: Cross-dimer Tm, 3′ end [°C]: primer3's limit for the 3′-end dimer: the configuration that extends. Unset keeps the preset's value. In °C. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_max_prod_len_diff.description: Band spread (range) [bp]: Products in one tube must differ by no more than this, so one extension time suits them all. Unset keeps the preset's value. In bp. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_max_tm_diff.description: Primer Tm spread [°C]: Largest primer Tm difference allowed inside a tube: one annealing temperature has to work for every reaction in it. Unset keeps the preset's value. In °C. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_min_prod_len_diff.description: Band separation (ladder) [bp]: Products in one tube must differ by at least this much, or the bands co-migrate and you cannot tell which reaction worked. Unset keeps the preset's value. In bp. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_prim_prim_any.description: Primer–primer, anywhere [kcal/mol]: Any duplex between two primers. Not extendable on its own, but it takes primer out of the reaction. Unset keeps the preset's value. In kcal/mol. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_prim_prim_end1.description: Primer–primer, one 3′ end [kcal/mol]: One primer's 3′ end anneals anywhere on the other. Extendable, so it competes with the template. Unset keeps the preset's value. In kcal/mol. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_prim_prim_end2.description: Primer–primer, both 3′ ends [kcal/mol]: A blunt 3′–3′ dimer: each primer can extend on the other, so the pair consumes itself and makes a short artefact band. Unset keeps the preset's value. In kcal/mol. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_prim_prod_any.description: Primer–product, anywhere [kcal/mol]: Any duplex between a primer and another reaction’s amplicon. Unset keeps the preset's value. In kcal/mol. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoff_prim_prod_end1.description: Primer–product, 3′ end [kcal/mol]: A primer's 3′ end annealing inside another reaction's amplicon: it primes on the wrong molecule. Unset keeps the preset's value. In kcal/mol. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

cutoffs_off.description: cutoffs to switch off (not applied at all), whatever the preset says. Only applies when pool is true. Advanced.

include_subject.description: screen against the node's subject as a template.

limit.description: minimum 3' footprint match for a primer to be considered bound (pydna's own default is 16). In bp.

max_groups.description: most tubes the pool may be split into. Only applies when pool is true.

max_per_group.description: most reactions one tube may hold. Only applies when pool is true.

max_size.description: largest product to report. In bp.

min_size.description: smallest product to report. In bp.

pool.description: also partition the screened reactions into compatible tubes (MultiPLX grouping), judged by the preset and cutoffs below.

pool_preset.description: which authority's limits a tube is judged by: MultiPLX's three stringencies, or primer3's own structural limits (calibrated for the ΔG engine computing the scores). Only applies when pool is true.

primers.description: the primer pool — literal sequences, or wire primer outputs from upstream design nodes.

templates.description: extra templates to screen against — wire records or name library documents (the subject is included by default).

name: multiplex_pcr

amplicons.description: every predicted product (which pair, which template, what size)

crossDimers.description: all-against-all primer-dimer matrix, or null with fewer than two primers

diagnostics.description: pairs that discriminate the templates by product size

dimerMap.description: the all-against-all dimer ΔG as a heatmap, the most stable structure each pair forms anywhere along the oligos

poolCount.description: with `pool` on: how many tubes the partition needed (0 when it refused)

pools.description: with `pool` on: the tubes, the per-tube verification, and a refusal naming the limit and pair that forced it when no partition fits
